verdict.rationale: FireHydrant's API reference explicitly claims UI parity: "anything you can do on the FireHydrant UI" can be done via the API. This is backed by token-based API keys that act like any other user with Owner permissions by default, and by a published OpenAPI 3.0.1 document whose operation tags span the wider API surface. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on verification that parity holds across every UI feature, and a per-feature mapping of UI actions to endpoints (the standard OpenAPI discovery paths on the docs site return 404).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: You can use the FireHydrant API to configure integrations, define incidents, and set up webhooks--anything you can do on the FireHydrant UI.
An API key can perform actions like any other user, and by default, it will have Owner permissions.
with operation tags across Call Routes, Permissions, Roles, Audit Events and the rest of the API surface
